title: perf-bench-log-jamie-chen
content:
Goal: quick personal scratchpad for perf runs I did for small/medium models to validate batching + quantization effects on latency/throughput. Not a polished report — TODO: synth into a proper doc for infra team.

Environment:
- Runtime: local dev cluster (dev-infer-01) running serving-runtime branch = perf/batching-experiments
- GPUs: 1x A100-80GB (driver 525.x), NVLink enabled (single node tests)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1
- Runtime config: kv-cache=true, async-batching=false (explicit batch tests toggled), prefetched weights, pinned-memory=true
- Model variants tested:
  * redwood-verified/7B (fp16, baseline)
  * redwood-verified/7B-qlora-4bit (q4_0 quantized)
content_continued:
* llama2-13B (fp16) — single-GPU baseline for comparison

Quick notes on methodology:
- Synthetic prompt workload (uniform token distribution) and a small set of real user prompts (~50) for tail latency checks. Sequence length: 512 tokens typical, also 1024 for stress tests.
- Each test = 3000 tokens generated across 1000 requests (varied batch sizes), warmup of 200 requests. Measured p50, p90, p99, and tokens/sec.
- Reported numbers are medians of 3 runs unless otherwise noted.

Run matrix (high level):
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32
- Seq lengths: 512, 1024
- Quantization: fp16 vs q4_0

Results (selected highlights) — A100 single-GPU:
1) redwood-verified/7B (fp16), seq=512:
- batch=1: p50=38ms, p90=74ms, p99=160ms, throughput=420 tok/s
- batch=4: p50=55ms, p90=98ms, p99=220ms, throughput=1200 tok/s
- batch=8: p50=85ms, p90=140ms, p99=320ms, throughput=2100 tok/s
- batch=16: p50=150ms, p90=260ms, p99=620ms, throughput=3600 tok/s
Notes: throughput scales sublinearly with batch due to KV-copy and memory pressure; latency jump after 8.

2) redwood-verified/7B-qlora-4bit (q4_0), seq=512:
- batch=1: p50=30ms, p90=60ms, p99=120ms, throughput=520 tok/s
- batch=4: p50=45ms, p90=80ms, p99=180ms, throughput=1500 tok/s
- batch=8: p50=72ms, p90=120ms, p99=280ms, throughput=2600 tok/s
Notes: quantized variant shows ~15-20% latency improvement at small batches and better throughput at mid batches. Memory headroom enables larger effective batches.

3) llama2-13B (fp16), seq=512 (baseline heavier model):
- batch=1: p50=95ms, p90=180ms, p99=420ms, throughput=180 tok/s
- batch=4: p50=180ms, p90=320ms, p99=760ms, throughput=740 tok/s
Notes: cost of larger model obvious — can't sustain low-latency single-request SLA on single A100 for interactive use.

Seq length=1024 observations:
- For 7B models, p50 roughly doubles, p90/p99 worse than linear (cache pressure). Throughput (tok/s) drops ~40–55%. Quantized runs still keep advantage but gap reduces slightly.

Batching vs async-batching:
- Re-ran a few 7B q4_0 tests with async-batching enabled (small batch max wait=8ms): observed 12–18% better p50 at batch=1 use-cases with similar throughput — promising for mixed traffic patterns. Need more stable runs.

Microprofiling notes (heatmap observations):
- Kernel time dominant during generation loops (not surprising). Attention kernel optimizations are effective for 7B fp16; quantized path uses different kernels with slightly better memory bandwidth utilization.
- Overheads: small but non-negligible time spent in request deserialization and KV-copy between host/GPU when batch>8. Consider pinned memory pool tuning and batched CUDA memcpy optimization.

Quick ASCII table (selected):
Model | Batch | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | tok/s
7B-fp16 | 1 | 38 | 74 | 420
7B-fp16 | 8 | 85 | 140 | 2100
7B-q4 | 1 | 30 | 60 | 520
7B-q4 | 8 | 72 | 120 | 2600
13B-fp16 | 1 | 95 | 180 | 180

Conclusions / actionable ideas (todo list):
- Quantization (q4_0) yields measurable perf wins for 7B-class in our runtime; prioritize adding q4 model variants to model catalog for cost-sensitive workloads.
- Tune pinned memory pool + batched memcpy path; suspected hotspot on KV-copy for >8 batches. File an infra ticket (JIRA-1299).
- Async-batching looks promising — need end-to-end A/B with real traffic profile to verify tail behavior and fairness.
- For interactive low-latency single-user experience, prefer 7B-quantized on A100 or dedicated lower-latency hardware; 13B needs dedicated capacity or multi-GPU sharding with optimized kernels.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Run identical matrix on T4 and RTX 8000 to understand edge infra cost profile (cheaper infra).
- Re-run with nvlink multi-GPU for 13B to explore sharded latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Capture full perf traces (nsight/CUPTI) for one run where batch=16 and seq=1024 to pinpoint memcpy stalls.

Scratch TODO (short):
- [ ] Upload plots to confluence (link above)
- [ ] Create PR with runtime memcpy pooling change (small patch)
- [ ] Schedule async-batching A/B test with traffic team

Random notes / reminders:
- Numbers are noisy; don't cite externally without full-run-repro.
- Save raw logs under s3://redwood-dev-perf/jamie/2026-02-15/ (I pushed a few; check permissions).

End of scratchpad.
